assumptions_override: Intervals are two-element lists of integers; comparisons, indexing, and two-element message formatting are O(1). Exclude input and returned merged output from auxiliary space. Include the sorted copy and Timsort temporary buffer.
rationale: Sorting the copied interval list takes O(n log n), dominating O(n) validation and merging. The validation error-message f-string is built on each iteration but is O(1) per interval under the two-element contract. Excluding the returned merged list and interval copies, sorted_intervals uses O(n) references and Timsort can use O(n) temporary storage; auxiliary space is O(n).

Sorting n value/weight pairs costs O(n log n). The comprehensions, prefix accumulation and slice sum are O(n), while bisect is O(log n); sorting dominates. The sorted pairs, rebuilt lists, prefix list, and temporary slice use O(n) auxiliary space. These labels assume vl and wt both have length n and the n argument matches; zip otherwise truncates, and work follows len(vl).

assumptions_override: Analyze one call on a DAG with dense vertex IDs 0..V-1, valid adjacency endpoints, a fresh all-zero visited list of length V, and an empty module-global stack. Reset these states before a repeated call. Each vertex is marked before descent. The recursive implementation may exceed Python recursion limits on deep graphs; scoring uses n=V+E.
rationale: Each vertex is marked before descent and each adjacency entry is checked once, so time is O(V+E). The recursive call stack alone can reach V frames, so auxiliary space is O(V); the global stack also grows to O(V) as result storage and does not change the bound. A repeated call with already-marked visited state skips prior vertices. Deep graphs can fail at the Python recursion limit.

The sentinel bounds the unsuccessful search to at most n inspected entries; the null-key helper is also a linear scan. Time is O(n) worst case and only a saved element and index are stored, so auxiliary space is O(1). The method temporarily mutates and restores the input, but does not restore it in a finally block if compareTo throws; it also assumes a consistent comparator. These are correctness/robustness caveats, not complexity changes.

assumptions: Input is an int array of length n. k=max(array)-min(array)+1 is positive and representable within Java array-size limits. Exclude the input and the returned n-element result array from auxiliary space; count the k-element histogram. For the coarse evaluator class assume k=O(n). Treat fixed-width integer operations and array access as O(1).
rationale: Time remains O(n+k): summaryStatistics scans n values, histogram/reconstruction take O(n), and cumulative counting takes O(k). The returned res array has n entries and is output; the only size-dependent auxiliary structure is the k-entry count array, so auxiliary space is O(k). Total additional storage counting output is O(n+k). Under k=O(n), the coarse auxiliary-space scoring class stays O(n). The stated range assumption excludes integer overflow in max-min+1.
